controls: Use warning limits for emerging drift and action limits for out-of-specification drift requiring correction.
Treating every warning as immediate failure or ignoring alarms
Allow them only when certified with that approach and record every correction.
QAL3 zero and span checks use gases or surrogates
Require suitable references; gases should be traceable and dust surrogates validated through MCERTS testing.
Using unstable or unvalidated reference materials
Use 80% to 100% of the short-term ELV as the documented starting point unless another justified value applies.
Checking only at an uninformative low concentration
CEMS and data systems support QAL3
Record positive and negative values, changes from prior checks and more than one year of zero/span data.
Losing trend history needed to detect drift
Perform weekly zero and span checks.
Using an interval too long for the selected chart
Base frequency on certified maintenance intervals and shorten initially until evidence supports extension.
Lengthening checks before sufficient data exist
Span readings remain within chart limits
Do not adjust; require several readings beyond action limits before minor adjustment.
Take at least five readings before and five after replacement and establish the step change/new baseline.
Mistaking cylinder concentration difference for instrument drift
Determine standard deviation under anticipated stack conditions and derive warning/action limits from it.
Using laboratory-only variance for field control
Include configuration changes, service/call-outs, maintenance, corrective actions, resets and zero/span plots and tables.
An annual surveillance test is performed
Use it to verify continuing validity of the existing calibration function, not to bypass QA.
Treating AST as a generic maintenance visit
Investigate the cause, perform corrective maintenance as needed and complete QAL2 afterward.
Returning failed CEMS to compliance reporting without recalibration
An AST fails and a subsequent QAL2 is performed
Generate separate AST and QAL2 reports.
Merging evidence so the failure trail disappears
Record the failure and investigation summary in the CEMS maintenance log.
An AST failure root cause is assessed
Review historic AST, functional-test, QAL3, service and SRM performance evidence.
Diagnosing from the current test alone
An AST parallel-reference campaign is designed
Use at least five valid parallel SRM tests and collect extras where invalidation risk exists.
Passing an AST with insufficient evidence
Base it on parallel SRM tests and exclude reference-material-only data.
Inflating the AST dataset with non-stack references
AST data support a calibration-range extension
Require data within the 95% confidence interval and cap extension at measured calibrated maximum plus 10%, not above 50% ELV.
Extending calibration beyond demonstrated AST evidence
A functional leak test is conducted
Test the entire sampling system according to the CEMS manual.
Log them through the DAHS and confirm instrument output equals the stored value.

A CEMS linearity test is performed
Use zero plus approximately 20%, 40%, 60% and 80% levels in a randomised sequence with required repetitions.
Using too few or ordered points that conceal hysteresis
DAHS handles and reports CEMS data
Apply EN 17255-4 for ongoing DAHS quality assurance and control.

Applying a gas concentration standard to flow
Particulate matter is measured by CEMS
A dust arrestment monitor is considered
Apply EN 17389 for calibration and do not use it as an EN 14181 compliance CEMS where prohibited.
Substituting a plant-control monitor for compliance monitoring
A long-term sampler produces a continuous sample
Report a time-averaged laboratory result and do not label it instantaneous.
Misrepresenting delayed analysis as real-time data

Apply CEN TS 17286 and its installed-system performance checks.

Use flow-proportional sampling and a stated laboratory technique; note that periodic-method principles apply where no published LTS standard exists.
A predictive emissions monitoring system is used
Apply CEN TS 17198 and maintain the model/process-parameter basis for predicted emissions.
Treating an undocumented model as direct measurement
Limit it to periodic compliance, installed-CEMS verification/calibration or temporary backup under its certification scope.
Treating T-CEMS as a permanently installed CEMS
